The Add instruction performs the operation the name implies. The instruction format is:
ADD.SIZE SOURCE,DESTINATION
Data Registers Dn+Eq Dn Dn 0 0 0 REGISTER #
D0 0 0 0 0 0 0 - Byte An 0 0 1 REGISTER #
D1 0 0 1 0 0 1 - Word (An) 0 1 0 REGISTER #
D2 0 1 0 0 1 0 - Lword (An)+ 0 1 1 REGISTER #
D3 0 1 1 Eq + Dn Eq -(An) 1 0 0 REGISTER #
D4 1 0 0 1 0 0 - Byte d(An) 1 0 1 REGISTER #
Size is B, W or L (byte size, word size or longword size). This instruction can be used in two configurations, either the source is a data register or the destination is a data register.
When the first and second values are added together, the result is stored in the destination.
In the condition codes of the status register, the carry bit (C) is set if a carry is generated from the addition, if not, it is cleared.
The extend bit (X) is set to the same value as the carry bit. The overflow bit (V) is set if an overflow condition occurs; otherwise, it is cleared.
The overflow bit is used when using signed numbers. If the most significant bit of an answer changes from a carry, then this bit indicates that the answer won't be correct.
The zero bit (Z) is set to 1 if the result of the addition is zero. The negative bit is set if the most significant bit is one, if not, it is cleared.

The CMP instruction is Compare command. The instruction format is: CMP.SIZE SOURCE,DATA REGISTER
Data Registers Dn+Eq Dn Dn 0 0 0 REGISTER #
D0 0 0 0 0 0 0 - Byte An 0 0 1 REGISTER #
D1 0 0 1 0 0 1 - Word (An) 0 1 0 REGISTER #
D2 0 1 0 0 1 0 - Lword (An)+ 0 1 1 REGISTER #
D3 0 1 1 Eq + Dn Eq -(An) 1 0 0 REGISTER #

Size is B, W or L (byte size, word size or longword size). The source can be any of the allowed addressing modes indicated in the table, whereas, the destination can only be a data register.
The compare command is used to see if two values are the same. The source is subtracted from the value in the data register and sets the condition codes based on the result.

It is important to note that the value of this subtraction is not saved because all we are doing is comparing the two values. In the condition codes of the status register, the carry bit (C) is set if a borrow is generated, or cleared, if not.
The overflow bit (V) is set if an overflow condition occurs, otherwise, it is cleared. The zero bit (Z) is set to 1 if the result of the subtraction is zero.
The negative bit (N) is set if the most significant bit is one, if not, it is cleared. The extend bit (X) remains unchanged.

A one in the zero bit and a zero in the carry bit indicates the values being compared are the same, a one in the carry bit indicates that the first value is larger, and a zero in both the carry and the zero bit indicates that the second value is larger.

Size is word size. The 32-bit value of the specified data register is divided by the 16-bit value of the source.
This method, unsigned, indicates that the microprocessor will assume that the data is positive. Negative twos-complement values will be treated as positive numbers.
One of three conditions will occur: a divide by zero error can occur, the division causes an overflow (answer greater than16-bits), or a normal division will occur.
If normal division occurs the destination will contain the 16-bit answer in the lower word of the data register and the remainder in the upper word.
If an overflow condition occurs, both the source and destination remain unchanged. In the condition codes of the status register, the carry bit (C) is always set to zero.

The overflow bit (V) is set if an overflow condition occurs, otherwise, it is cleared. The zero bit (Z) is set to 1 if the result of the division is zero, however, if an overflow occurs, the value is unknown.
